meta.title: A 0.8B model vs Jev at Pac-Man
meta.description: In the same Pac-Man game, a 795 MB model eats more than twice as many pellets as Jev and runs offline on a phone. Build your own model instead of only using one.

hero.title: A 0.8B model eats twice as many pellets as Jev, and runs offline on a phone
hero.subtitle: Same Pac-Man game, same text input. No player sees the screen, only a few lines of text.
hero.note: One 30-second game each. Over 10 games: Jev {jev_avg} pellets on average, our 0.8B {ours_avg}.

play.title: Try it yourself
play.lead: Same run, 30 seconds. See where you rank against the models.
play.eyes_hint: No graphics. You only see the text lines that the models receive at each intersection.
play.result_title: Time's up. You ate {pellets} pellets: #{rank} of {total}.
play.controls_hint: Use arrow keys, WASD, or swipe to turn.
play.eyes_waiting: Pac-Man is waiting at the junction. Pick a way.

halo.title: It is not that mysterious
halo.lead: Take an ordinary open-source model with zero decision training and constrain its output. It plays about as well as Jev.
halo.chart_note: Off-the-shelf models and hand-crafted rules cluster between 148 and 232. Our 0.8B reaches 425. All players read the exact same text prompts.
halo.offline_body: No network needed, and it runs on a phone. This is a screen recording from an iPhone.

paths.title: Still not satisfied? Two paths forward
paths.lead: Two different paths, each with its own trade-offs.
paths.a_body: Fine-tuning is no silver bullet, but it lets you make deliberate trade-offs across size, speed, cost, domain, and intelligence.
paths.b_body: Switch to a bigger model and let it think. When the game waits for it, a 27B model goes from {off} to {on} pellets, at about 2.4 seconds per move.

recipe.note: That is the trade-off: on 194 general decision questions unrelated to Pac-Man, it fell from 0.66 to 0.53. It was built for this one task.

builder.title: From passive user to builder
builder.closed_body: You use them when they work. When they fail, your only choice is switching providers.
builder.yours_body: Size, speed, cost, domain, and intelligence: you can adjust every single dial yourself.
builder.quote: Being able to build and choosing not to is very different from having no other choice.

cta.title: Ready to move from user to builder?
cta.body: The course walks you through the entire pipeline on your own task: pick a task, select a teacher, label data, train, and deploy to mobile.

footer.run_title: Run it on your own machine
footer.notebook: Lab notebook: over a dozen experiments
footer.fineprint: Results are for this one game, 10 games per player. Realtime scores vary from run to run.
